title: streaming-lifecycle-controls: robust reconnect/resume and server timeout handling (openai-compat)
author: Anjali Rao
description: Motivation: Improve streaming stability when clients cancel, disconnect, or reconnect; make server-side timeout boundaries and resume semantics deterministic; ensure OpenAI compatibility for reconnect/resume behavior. This change addresses several customer reports where long-running streams would either leak server-side resources after client disconnect or fail to resume correctly under the OpenAI-compatible protocol. Changes include: 1) explicit stream lifecycle state machine on the server with deterministic transitions for ClientCancel -> ServerCleanup, Disconnect -> GracefulSuspend -> Resume, and Timeout -> ForcedAbort; 2) a reconnect/resume handshake that preserves KV cache and partial outputs when allowed by policy; 3) configurable server-side idle and resume timeouts with sensible defaults tuned for production workloads; 4) OpenAI-compat mode tweaks to the reconnect handshake and status codes so existing integrations resume without changes. Checklist: - [x] Add lifecycle state machine and tests - [x] Implement resume handshake and server-side resume store - [x] Wire configurable timeouts (env + per-route) - [x] Update streaming OpenAI-compat layer behavior and docs - [x] Add unit/integration tests for disconnect/resume/timeouts - [x] Run perf canary and memory leak regression tests Related: ENG-1234 (stream stability), ENG-1299 (openai-compat streaming). Notes: the description below includes a short summary of design, commits, files changed, review thread, and CI status.

performance_notes: Perf canary showed no regression on P50/P95 latency for 2k RPS workload; memory leak tests show stable RSS across 1 hour; resume_store adds ~2% memory overhead under heavy reconnect churn.
observability_changes: Added streaming_resume_attempts and streaming_resume_success metrics; added labels for resume_reason (client_cancel, disconnect, timeout) and resumed_from_snapshot boolean.
migration_notes: No DB migrations. Resume store uses optional Redis backend; default is in-memory on single-node setups. Operators should set resume_store_backend=redis for multi-node Durable resume behavior.
release_notes:
- Streaming lifecycle: improved reconnect/resume semantics and server-side timeout controls.
- Added per-route resume_timeout_seconds (default 120s).
- OpenAI-compat: reconnect handshake and status mapping improved (should be transparent to clients).
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approvals and CI green. Change is behind feature flag 'streaming_resume_v2' (default enabled for main) to allow staged rollout. No follow-up PR required; ops note created for redis rollout if customers enable durable resume.
